bottom_line: Mepolizumab — METREO. Stated failure: Phase III: primary comparisons did not meet multiplicity-adjusted significance. METREX was mixed/positive in its eosinophilic population and is not counted as a separate failure here. Diagnosis (claim 1.2, supported): For mepolizumab 100 mg versus placebo, the primary analysis rate ratio was 0.80 (95% CI 0.65–0.98) with p=0.068, missing statistical significance at the conventional 0.05 threshold.

question: Why did mepolizumab fail in METREO for COPD, and which patients might respond?
raw: Mepolizumab failed METREO’s primary endpoint because neither dose met multiplicity-adjusted significance: 100 mg versus placebo had rate ratio 0.80 (95% CI 0.65–0.98, p=0.068) [2], and 300 mg had rate ratio 0.86 (95% CI 0.70–1.05, p=0.14) [3]. The curated record labels the program negative after adjustment and notes inconsistent broader COPD evidence [4]. Pooled METREX/METREO evidence suggested greater benefit with higher blood eosinophils, and MATINEE subsequently confirmed benefit [5, 11]. Patients with higher blood eosinophils might respond [12], though this remains hypothesis-generating. Lines do not show the eosinophil threshold, subgroup p-values, or causal mechanism.
